title: Influence of Rheumatologists on Therapy Adherence in Patients with Inflammatory Rheumatic Diseases – The Prospective Multicenter DRAMA Study
summary:
This study investigates whether the duration and quality of medical counseling sessions influence how reliably patients take their medication for inflammatory rheumatic diseases.**
Adults who are starting a specific therapy for the first time can participate. The goal is to improve patient education and promote long-term therapy adherence.
conditions: Inflammatory rheumatic diseases, specifically seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and axial spondyloarthritis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cohort 1: cDMARD Cohort
Minimum age 18 years, first-time initiation of a conventional synthetic DMARD (administered subcutaneously or orally), outpatient follow-up visits every 3 months, confirmed diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis or psoriatic arthritis, sufficient language skills to understand the informed consent.

Cohort 2: bDMARD Cohort
Minimum age 18 years, first-time initiation of a subcutaneously administered biological DMARD, outpatient follow-up visits every 3 months, confirmed diagnosis of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, or axial spondyloarthritis, sufficient language skills to understand the informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
None
